claim: Holding author and URL constant, wording alone predicts which of two tweets gets more retweets with 65.6% held-out accuracy (humans 61.3%); a model trained on uncontrolled data reaches only ~55-56%.
sample_size: 11,404 same-author same-URL pairs (+1,770 held out); 632K identical pairs for confound checks
design: Natural experiment: same author, same URL, different wording
relevance: Wording matters but modestly; a startup rewriting its launch post should expect a small edge, not a multiplier.
testable_trait: Same-author posts linking the same URL/quoting same item with different text: which got more reposts
note: Opened ar5iv full text.

claim: In same-author same-URL pairs, explicitly asking to share ('retweet', 'rt', 'spread', 'please') is associated with the more-retweeted version.
relevance: Explicit share requests worked in 2012-13 Twitter; norms have shifted, so test before recommending.
testable_trait: Presence of share-request tokens (rt, retweet, repost, share, spread, pls/please)
note: Direction verified from full text; no single effect size reported in what I read.

claim: In author-controlled pairs, more informative wording (longer text, more verbs/adjectives, proper nouns and numbers) wins; informativeness was the strongest hand-built feature group (~63% accuracy for custom features alone).
relevance: Favours launch posts that state concrete specifics (named things, numbers) over vague teasers.
testable_trait: Character/word count; count of digits/numeric tokens; count of capitalised proper nouns; POS counts
note: Opened full text.

claim: In author-controlled pairs, adding @-mentions is associated with FEWER retweets, although authors frequently add them when rewording.
relevance: Tagging many accounts in a launch post may hurt broadcast spread (2014 data; mention semantics have changed).
testable_trait: Number of @-mentions in post text (excluding reply prefix)
note: Opened full text.

claim: In author-controlled pairs, wording that resembles news headlines, matches general Twitter language, is easier to read, and carries sentiment (positive or negative) outperforms.
relevance: Plain, headline-like, non-neutral phrasing for the first line of a launch post.
testable_trait: Readability score; sentiment-word presence; language-model perplexity of first line
note: Opened full text.

claim: Identical tweets from the same author get closely matching retweet counts only when posted within 12 hours by accounts with >5,000 followers (r=0.853 vs 0.305 otherwise): timing and audience noise dominate for small accounts.
relevance: For small startup accounts, outcome variance from luck/timing is large; do not over-read a single post's result.
testable_trait: Variance in engagement across near-duplicate posts by the same author; stratify by follower count
note: Opened full text.

claim: Tweets squeezed to fit the old 140-character limit were more successful than similar-length tweets written after the limit was lifted; in experiments, cutting a 250-char tweet by 10-20% is optimal and cuts up to 30-40% still beat the original.
sample_size: 2019: 60 original tweets x 9 target lengths, crowd-rated (sample from memory); 2018: large tweet sample around Nov 2017 switch
design: 2018 natural experiment around 140->280 switch; 2019 randomized crowd experiment
relevance: Tighten the launch post: trim ~10-20% of words rather than padding to the limit.
testable_trait: Character count; for same-author posts, relation between length and engagement
note: Findings verified via search snippet of abstracts; exact 2019 tweet count is from memory.

claim: In Upworthy headline A/B tests, each additional negative word raised click-through by about 2.3% for an average-length headline, and positive words lowered it; sadness (not anger) drove clicks.
source: Robertson, Prollochs, Schwarzenegger, Parnamets, Van Bavel & Feuerriegel 2023, Nature Human Behaviour
sample_size: ~105,000 headline variations; ~5.7M clicks over >370M impressions (N=22,743 RCTs in registered-report stage)
relevance: Negativity lifts clicks on news headlines; transfer to product launches is doubtful and outcome is clicks, not shares.
testable_trait: Count of negative vs positive lexicon words in post text
note: Dataset sizes verified via snippet; the 2.3% figure is from memory of the abstract (publisher page blocked).

claim: Across Upworthy experiments, headline language effects on clicks are real but small and much popular headline advice does not hold up; registered-report results favour longer headlines and negative emotion.
source: Gligoric, Lifchits, West & Anderson 2023, PLOS ONE (Registered Report); Banerjee & Urminsky 2025, Marketing Science
relevance: Do not trust generic 'headline hacks'; effects are small and context-dependent.
testable_trait: First-line length; negative-emotion words; pronoun use
note: Existence, design and N verified; specific directional findings (longer, negative) are from memory. Banerjee & Urminsky: Marketing Science 44(3):566-592, DOI 10.1287/mksc.2021.0018, verified to exist; I could not verify its concreteness result.

claim: Across 141,000 headline A/B tests at 293 news sites, winning headlines lifted click-through by 20%+ but lessons from one test generalised poorly to other stories; most of the click decision is outside the writer's control.
source: Hagar, Diakopoulos & DeWilde 2021, Digital Journalism ('Anticipating Attention')
design: Analysis of randomized A/B tests plus predictive model
relevance: Testing variants of a specific post is worth more than applying generic rules.
testable_trait: n/a (supports A/B approach); variance in engagement across same-author variants
note: Via Nieman Lab summary in search results. The 2019 Hagar & Diakopoulos paper is an interview study, not the 141k analysis.

claim: An LLM-plus-bandit method (LOLA) picks Upworthy headlines that beat standard A/B testing by ~8-9% and UCB bandits by 6-7% in clicks when traffic is limited: pure LLM prediction of winners is useful but imperfect.
relevance: Supports a product that scores draft posts with a model and then updates on observed engagement.
testable_trait: n/a (method)
note: Numbers from arXiv v1 snippets; later versions may differ.

claim: NYT articles evoking high-arousal emotions (awe, anger, anxiety) were more likely to make the most-emailed list; low-arousal sadness reduced it (roughly +34% odds per SD of anger, +30% per SD of awe).
source: Berger & Milkman 2012, Journal of Marketing Research
design: Observational with placement controls; lab experiments for causality
controlled_for_account: partly: controls for placement/author fame; experiments randomized
relevance: High-arousal framing (awe at a demo) plausibly aids sharing; field data are ~7k articles (email sharing, not reposts), backed by lab experiments showing arousal is causal.
testable_trait: Lexicon scores for awe/anger/anxiety/sadness in text
note: Design and direction verified via snippet; the 34%/30% per-SD figures are from memory.

claim: Each moral-emotional word in a political tweet was associated with ~20% more retweets in the original study; a pre-registered replication found 15% and a 27-study meta-analysis 12% (IRR 1.12, CI 1.06-1.19).
source: Brady, Wills, Jost, Tucker & Van Bavel 2017, PNAS; Brady et al. 2025, PNAS Nexus
controlled_for_account: no (covariates such as follower count only)
relevance: Effect is specific to political/moralised topics; weak guidance for product launches.
testable_trait: Count of moral-emotional lexicon words
note: Via search snippets.

claim: CONFLICT: Re-analysis found the moral-contagion model predicts no better out-of-sample than an arbitrary 'XYZ contagion' model (counting the letters X, Y, Z), warning that such large correlational effects may be artefacts.
source: Burton, Cruz & Hahn 2021, Nature Human Behaviour
sample_size: Re-analysis of Brady et al. data plus additional corpora
relevance: Treat single-lexicon 'word X adds Y% reposts' claims with suspicion; require out-of-sample tests in our corpus.
testable_trait: Placebo lexicon test: does an arbitrary token count predict as well as the trait of interest?
note: Via search snippet.

claim: Each word referring to the political out-group raised the odds of a post being shared by 67%; out-group language was ~4.8x as strong a predictor as negative-affect language.
source: Rathje, Van Bavel & van der Linden 2021, PNAS
sample_size: 2,730,215 posts from news media and US Congress accounts
relevance: Analogue for startups is naming a rival/incumbent; evidence is political, so only a hypothesis here.
testable_trait: Mentions (by name or @) of competitor/incumbent brands
note: Via search snippet.

claim: Emotionally charged political tweets (positive or negative) are retweeted more often and more quickly than neutral ones.
source: Stieglitz & Dang-Xuan 2013, Journal of Management Information Systems
relevance: Neutral corporate tone underperforms; add evaluative language.
testable_trait: Sentiment intensity (absolute) of text; time to first N reposts
note: Via search snippet.

claim: Negative tweets spread faster but positive tweets reach larger audiences (more retweets and favourites).
sample_size: Sample size not verified (large random sample; ~19M tweets from memory)
relevance: For launches, positive framing likely yields larger total reach than negative framing.
testable_trait: Sentiment polarity vs total reposts and vs early velocity
note: Findings verified via abstract snippet; sample size from memory.

claim: False news was ~70% more likely to be retweeted than true news and was measurably more novel relative to what users had recently seen; novelty is the proposed mechanism.
design: Observational with account controls (age, activity, followers)
relevance: Novelty (genuinely new capability/information) is a spread driver; 'first to show X' framing.
testable_trait: Novelty of post text vs prior corpus (e.g., embedding distance from author's and topic's earlier posts)
note: 126k/3M verified; 70% via secondary summary in search results.

claim: Reducing positive (or negative) posts in Facebook feeds shifted users' own posting in the same direction, but the effect was tiny (d on the order of 0.001-0.02).
relevance: Emotional contagion exists but is negligible in size; not a lever for a launch post.
testable_trait: n/a
note: N and direction verified; effect-size magnitude from memory. Paper carries an Editorial Expression of Concern (consent).

claim: After correcting for selection, merely including an image raises engagement on Twitter; images with a human face lift engagement measures by 38% to 291% on Twitter (not on Instagram); professional-quality images help on both; image-text fit helps on Twitter.
source: Li & Xie 2020, Journal of Marketing Research 57(1):1-19
sample_size: Three datasets (two Twitter, one Instagram) of airline and SUV brand-related posts; counts not verified
relevance: Attach an image that matches the text; a human face may help on X; polished screenshots/product shots over low-quality images.
testable_trait: has_image; has_video; (if image features available) face present; otherwise media type only
note: 38-291% face effect and mere-presence effect verified via search snippets; dataset counts not verified, so the grade could be 'small observational' if under 10k posts.

claim: Across four local accounts, multimedia tweets raised likes/retweets for two accounts and had no significant effect for the other two.
relevance: Media benefit is account-dependent; test per author rather than assume.
testable_trait: Within-author difference in engagement for media vs text-only posts
note: Via search snippet.

claim: On 2023 Twitter, accounts using more media were associated with LOWER exposure in the algorithmic feed relative to chronological, except for video.
sample_size: 806 participants (376 balanced); ~205k exposures to 171k tweets from 63.4k accounts; 2,667 accounts in regression
design: Within-user comparison of algorithmic vs reverse-chronological feed; authors say not necessarily causal
relevance: Conflicts with Li & Xie: on the ranked feed, images did not buy extra amplification; video was the exception.
testable_trait: Media type (none/image/video/GIF) vs views-per-follower
note: Opened arXiv HTML.

claim: Twitter's saliency-based auto-crop showed systematic disparities and was withdrawn in favour of user-controlled/full image display.
relevance: Minor: design images so key content survives timeline aspect ratios; no engagement effect measured.
testable_trait: n/a (image aspect ratio if available)
note: Qualitative finding verified; no engagement outcome.

claim: Audio-only posts drew more engagement than text and video tweets from the same users.
source: Li & Ensafjoo 2024, Journal of Radio & Audio Media
relevance: Format effects can be counter-intuitive; weak evidence, niche format.
testable_trait: Media type within author
note: Via search snippet only; details not verified.

claim: GAP: I found no peer-reviewed study isolating GIFs, product-demo videos or screenshots on X with author controls; industry claims (e.g., Twitter's 'video 6x more retweets than photos') are unaudited.
source: Search result: Social Media Today reporting Twitter claims
relevance: Demo-video advice for AI launches rests on practitioner lore; this is a prime thing to test in the corpus.
testable_trait: Media type = video vs image vs none, within author, for launch-type posts
note: Verified that the claim exists and is described as speculative; absence of studies is a search limitation.

claim: On X, original posts with external links had a median views-per-follower score ~8x lower (Ukraine-Russia set: 0.033 vs 0.246) and ~4x lower (2024 US election set: 0.012 vs 0.056) than posts without links; quote tweets and links to other platforms sat in between.
sample_size: 17M+ tweets/5.2M users (1.8M original posts analysed) and ~34.8M posts/3.8M users (7.2M originals)
design: Observational; views normalised by follower count
controlled_for_account: partly: normalised by followers, not same-author
relevance: Strongest quantitative support for 'put the link in a reply / avoid bare link in launch post'. Topic is politics, not tech.
testable_trait: has_external_link vs views/followers; link-in-first-reply by same author if detectable from thread structure
note: Opened arXiv HTML v4.

claim: Twitter's 2020 algorithmic timeline drastically reduced exposure to tweets with external links compared with the chronological timeline (about 51% -> 18% of tweets), while increasing account diversity.
source: Bandy & Diakopoulos 2021, CSCW ('More Accounts, Fewer Links')
sample_size: 8 sock-puppet accounts, timelines sampled twice daily for one month
controlled_for_account: yes: same puppet, algorithmic vs chronological
relevance: Link suppression predates Musk-era X; consistent with K01 and K03.
testable_trait: has_external_link vs views/followers
note: 'Drastically decreases external links' verified; 51%->18% figure from memory.

claim: In Feb 2023 feeds, heavier use of external links was the strongest account-level predictor of LOST exposure in the algorithmic vs chronological feed (p<0.001).
relevance: Third independent source for the link penalty.
testable_trait: Share of an author's posts with links vs views/followers
note: Opened arXiv HTML.

claim: In 2009-10 Twitter, URLs and hashtags were positively associated with being retweeted: 21.1% of tweets but 28.4% of retweets had URLs; 10.1% of tweets but 20.8% of retweets had hashtags; follower count mattered, tweet count did not.
source: Suh, Hong, Pirolli & Chi 2010, IEEE SocialCom
relevance: CONFLICT with K01-K03: links helped in chronological-era Twitter and hurt in ranked-feed X. Hashtag benefit is 2010-era and topic-specific.
testable_trait: has_hashtag, n_hashtags, has_link vs repost rate
note: Percentages from the authors' PARC blog via search snippet.

claim: For predicting whether a tweet is retweeted, social/author features dominate, with tweet-content features adding a substantial but secondary boost.
relevance: Who posts matters more than what; distribution/author first, copy second.
testable_trait: Variance explained by author followers vs content traits
note: Abstract-level claim verified; sample size not.

claim: Practitioner analysis claimed tweets containing 'please retweet' were retweeted ~4x as often (51% vs 12%).
relevance: Lore-grade; the controlled support is W02. URL given is Tan et al., which discusses share requests; I did not fetch Zarrella's report.
testable_trait: Share-request tokens
note: From memory; Zarrella's report was not fetched. URL points to Tan et al., the controlled study of the same trait (see W02).

claim: Overt persuasion/advertising-style brand posts depress engagement on Facebook; persuasion-related content characteristics were the most important drivers.
source: Stephen, Sciandra & Inman 2015, MSI/SSRN working paper
relevance: Launch posts that read like ads ('Buy now', hype adjectives) under-engage.
testable_trait: Promotional-token density (buy, sign up, limited, discount); imperative CTAs
note: Via search snippet; CTA-specific result not verified.

claim: A tweet's median half-life (time to half of its eventual impressions) is ~80 minutes (79.5); impressions per second peak ~72 seconds after posting, and ~95% of tweets get no meaningful impressions after 24 hours.
relevance: The first 1-2 hours decide a launch post; schedule when the target audience is online and line up early engagement.
testable_trait: Share of final engagement accrued in first N minutes (needs time series); post hour-of-day vs views/followers
note: Via search snippet of abstract/PDF.

claim: Scheduling a newspaper's social posts to match audience sleep-wake cycles (mornings best overall; high-arousal emotional content in the morning, 'deep' content in the afternoon) could raise profits by at least 8%; optimal inter-post gap was ~30-90 minutes.
source: Kanuri, Chen & Sridhar 2018, Journal of Marketing 82(6):89-108
sample_size: One publisher, ~1 year of posts (count not verified)
design: Single-account observational model + optimisation; outcome = link clicks
relevance: Time-of-day matters within an account, interacts with content type; outcome is clicks.
testable_trait: Local posting hour (audience time zone) x content type vs engagement, within author
note: 8% profit and 30-90 min via search snippets; sample size not verified.

claim: For AI-tool repos launched on Hacker News, posting hour was a key predictor of star gains ('hundreds of additional stars'), while the 'Show HN' tag gave no significant advantage after controls.
source: Kraishan 2025, arXiv 2511.04453 (single-author preprint, not peer reviewed)
design: Observational; Elastic Net and gradient boosting
relevance: AI-specific: launch timing matters more than labelling the post as a launch.
testable_trait: Posting hour/day-of-week; presence of launch-label tokens ('Introducing', 'Launching', 'Show')
note: Opened arXiv abstract page.

claim: Across a billion diffusion events, structural virality is typically low at every size: popularity is mostly driven by the largest single broadcast, not long person-to-person chains; large events occur ~1 in 1,000 and true viral hits ~1 in a million.
source: Goel, Anderson, Hofman & Watts 2016, Management Science 62(1)
relevance: Reach comes from one or a few big accounts reposting/quoting; target those rather than hoping for organic chains.
testable_trait: Max follower count among quoters/reposters where visible (quote relationships); share of engagement following the largest quoter
note: Via abstract snippet; rarity figures from a blog summary.

claim: Larger-follower users with past cascade success start larger cascades on average, but individual predictions are unreliable; the most cost-effective seeding uses many 'ordinary' influencers rather than a few stars.
relevance: Seed a launch with many mid-size relevant accounts instead of one celebrity.
testable_trait: Number and follower distribution of quoting accounts
note: Via search snippet.

claim: Even with full knowledge of author and content, the best models explain less than half the variance in cascade size (R2 ~0.4), and almost all of that comes from the author's past success, not content.
source: Martin, Hofman, Sharma, Anderson & Watts 2016, WWW
relevance: Sets expectation: a post-advice product can shift odds, not guarantee outcomes; baseline on the author's own history.
testable_trait: Engagement relative to author's trailing median (author-normalised outcome)
note: 'Less than half the variance' verified; R2 ~0.42 and sample size from memory.

claim: Whether a Facebook photo cascade will double in size can be predicted with ~80% accuracy (vs 50% chance), with temporal features (speed of early reshares) among the most predictive.
source: Cheng, Adamic, Dow, Kleinberg & Leskovec 2014, WWW
sample_size: One month of complete photo-reshare data (~150k photos from memory)
relevance: Early velocity is the best in-flight signal that a post will keep growing.
testable_trait: Early engagement velocity (needs timestamps of engagements; proxy: views/likes at fixed age)
note: 0.795 at k=5 seen in authors' slides via snippet; which feature class is best is conflicting in secondary sources.

claim: Log early popularity predicts log final popularity nearly linearly: the first hours on Digg / first ~10 days on YouTube forecast 30-day popularity with high accuracy.
source: Szabo & Huberman 2010, Communications of the ACM (arXiv 0811.0405)
sample_size: 7,146 YouTube videos; all Digg stories Jul-Dec 2007
relevance: Early engagement both signals and (via ranking) causes later reach.
testable_trait: Early vs final engagement correlation in corpus
note: Via search snippet.

claim: In a randomized music market, showing others' download counts increased both inequality and unpredictability of success; a top-5 quality song had only ~50% chance of ending top-5.
relevance: Visible social proof makes outcomes path-dependent: early counts matter, and quality is no guarantee.
testable_trait: n/a directly; dispersion of outcomes among comparable posts
note: Via search snippet.

claim: A single random initial upvote made the next viewer 32% more likely to upvote and raised final scores by 25% on average; random downvotes were corrected by the crowd.
relevance: Best causal evidence that early positive engagement (friends/employees liking at launch) produces further organic engagement.
testable_trait: Early like count/velocity vs later engagement, holding author constant
note: 32%/25% verified via abstract snippet; comment count from memory.

claim: Random early support (a donation, award, signature or positive rating) significantly raised later support from others across Kickstarter, Wikipedia, Change.org and Epinions (e.g., seeded Kickstarter projects attracted more than twice the later donations), but 4x the seed did not produce proportionally more.
source: van de Rijt, Kang, Restivo & Patil 2014, PNAS 111(19)
sample_size: Four field experiments (e.g., 200 Kickstarter projects - from memory)
relevance: A small early push is enough; piling on more coordinated early engagement has diminishing returns.
testable_trait: Early engagement level vs later, look for saturation
note: Qualitative results and 'more than twice' verified; 200 projects and 39%->70% figures from memory, unverified.

claim: Instagram users who began routing ~50% of posts through engagement pods saw >5x more organic interaction on their NON-pod posts; pods were easy to join (only 4% had follower minimums).
source: Weerasinghe, Flanigan, Stein, McCoy & Greenstadt 2020, The Web Conference
relevance: Coordinated early engagement measurably works on a ranked feed, though it violates platform rules; legitimate analogue is team/investor/community early engagement.
testable_trait: Reply/like bursts in first minutes; cluster of same early engagers (not observable without engager IDs)
note: Via search snippet (paper + NYU release).

claim: Twitter's ranked home timeline amplified political content relative to a chronological control, with the mainstream right amplified more than the left in 6 of 7 countries.
source: Huszar, Ktena, O'Brien, Belli, Schlaikjer & Hardt 2022, PNAS
sample_size: ~2M daily active accounts in chronological control; 3,634 politicians; 6.2M news articles
relevance: Proves ranking, not just followers, determines reach; mechanism not content-specific for startups.
testable_trait: n/a
note: Via search snippet.

claim: In a pre-registered audit, Twitter's engagement ranking over-selected emotionally charged and out-group-hostile tweets (e.g., anger 62% vs 52%, out-group animosity 46% vs 38% of political tweets) even though users said they did not prefer them.
source: Milli, Carroll, Wang, Pandey, Zhao & Dragan 2025, PNAS Nexus (arXiv 2305.16941)
sample_size: 806 users; top-10 ranked vs 10 most recent tweets each
design: Within-user randomized/pre-registered audit of ranking vs chronological
relevance: The ranker rewards posts that provoke replies/strong reactions; a mild, non-hostile analogue is a pointed claim or contrast.
testable_trait: Reply-to-like ratio; anger/contrast lexicon vs views/followers
note: Design verified; percentages from a secondary summary in search results.

claim: Twitter's recommender amplified small and usually-quiet accounts and emotionally valenced/toxic tweets relative to chronological feeds.
relevance: Small accounts are not locked out: out-of-network recommendation can lift a startup's post.
testable_trait: Views/followers by follower-count band
note: Small-account finding from published abstract; toxicity finding appears in the preprint abstract.

claim: In Feb 2023 feeds, Twitter Blue accounts showed NO significant exposure gain in the algorithmic feed vs unverified (p=0.39); legacy-verified business accounts lost exposure (p<0.001); log follower count had no significant effect; accounts posting 'agitating' content gained.
relevance: Official brand accounts may be down-ranked relative to individuals: launch from the founder's account as well as/instead of the company handle.
testable_trait: Author type (company vs personal - not available without bios); verified flag if present
note: Opened arXiv HTML. Pre-dates X Premium reply/For You boosts.

claim: CONFLICT (industry, not peer reviewed): Buffer reports X Premium accounts get ~10x the reach per post of regular accounts in 2024-25.
relevance: Suggests Premium matters now, but subscribers self-select; no causal estimate exists in the academic literature I found.
testable_trait: Verified/Premium flag vs views/followers
note: Via search snippet; not peer reviewed.

claim: In brand posts, brand-personality content (humour, emotion) is associated with more likes/comments/shares; directly informative content (price, deals) lowers engagement alone but raises it when combined with personality content, and drives click-through.
design: Observational with content coding (MTurk+NLP) and correction for feed targeting
controlled_for_account: yes: firm fixed effects / EdgeRank correction
relevance: Core template for launch posts: lead with personality/emotion, then the concrete facts; facts alone get clicks but not spread.
testable_trait: Presence of price/deal/feature tokens AND emotion/humour tokens (interaction)
note: Via search snippet.

claim: Vivid/interactive brand posts and posts kept at the top of the page get more likes; drivers of likes differ from drivers of comments (questions raise comments, lower likes).
source: de Vries, Gensler & Leeflang 2012, Journal of Interactive Marketing 26(2):83-91
relevance: Pinning the launch post and choosing likes-vs-replies goal deliberately; small old sample.
testable_trait: Ends with question mark vs reply and like counts; media type
note: Sample and top-position finding verified; vivid/question details from memory.

claim: Emotional ads are shared more, informative ads improve brand evaluation and purchase intent; emotional ads where the brand is integral to the story achieve both.
source: Akpinar & Berger 2017, Journal of Marketing Research 54(2):318-330
relevance: Make the product the hero of the emotional/wow moment (e.g., the demo IS the story), not a logo tacked on.
testable_trait: Product name appears in first line vs only at end; demo media present
note: Via abstract snippet; no effect sizes verified.

claim: For video ads, information-focused appeals reduce sharing EXCEPT for new or high-priced (risky) products; positive emotions drive sharing; early/long brand prominence reduces sharing; 1.0-1.5 minutes is the best length; emotional ads share better on Twitter/Facebook, informational on LinkedIn.
source: Tellis, MacInnis, Tirunillai & Zhang 2019, Journal of Marketing 83(4)
platform: YouTube ads shared to Facebook, Twitter, Google+, LinkedIn
sample_size: Two field studies; 109 brands; 60+ ad characteristics
relevance: Important exception for startups: NEW products benefit from information. Demo videos ~60-90s, brand name late and brief.
testable_trait: Video duration (if available); position of brand/product name in text
note: Via AMA press summary in search results.

claim: On Product Hunt, products aimed at women grow roughly 40-45% less in the year after launch than comparable male-focused products, and the gap shrinks or disappears when more women happen to be active on launch day: who is online on launch day causally shapes growth.
source: Cao, Koning & Nanda 2021/2023, NBER WP 28882 (Management Science)
design: Natural experiment: exogenous daily variation in who is active
relevance: Who happens to see the launch on day one causally shapes long-run growth: audience-day fit matters.
testable_trait: Day-of-week/hour proxies for which audience is online
note: Paper, platform, SimilarWeb outcome and day-level identification verified via search snippet; the snippet stated the direction the other way round (male-focused grow less), which contradicts my memory of the paper. Direction and exact size unverified - check the PDF before using.

claim: Higher Product Hunt daily rank causally raises the chance of raising venture funding within six months, identified from vote noise and the strength of same-day rival launches.
source: Cao (R.) 2020 working paper, 'Information frictions in new venture finance'
relevance: Launch-day competition matters: avoid days when bigger launches crowd attention.
testable_trait: Number of competing same-topic launch posts in the same window (corpus-derived)
note: Via search snippet; effect size not verified.

claim: Among ~45K Kickstarter projects, specific phrases predicted funding beyond 59 control variables; successful pitches used reciprocity ('also receive two'), social proof and authority, while failing ones used pleading/uncertain language ('even a dollar', 'not been able').
relevance: Confident, concrete, give-something language beats pleading ('would mean a lot if you RT').
testable_trait: Pleading tokens (please, help us, would mean, any support) vs offer tokens (free, get, you'll receive)
note: N and principles via search snippets; phrase examples and exact predictive gain from memory.

claim: Tweet bursts mentioning an open-source repo cause ~7% more GitHub stars and ~2% more contributors on average; effects are larger for bigger bursts and when tweeters are project insiders.
source: Fang, Lamba, Herbsleb & Vasilescu 2022, ICSE (Distinguished Paper)
relevance: Directly relevant to open-source AI launches: tweets move stars modestly; concentrated bursts from several accounts beat a lone tweet.
testable_trait: Number of distinct accounts posting/quoting the same repo link within 24-48h
note: Via search snippets of paper/ICSE listing. Relevant to dev-tool startups; sample is general OSS, not AI-only.

claim: Popular GitHub projects gained a median 138 stars in the 3 days after a successful Hacker News post vs 74 in the 3 days before.
source: Borges & Valente 2019, 'How do developers promote open source projects?' IEEE Computer (arXiv 1908.04219)
sample_size: 100 popular projects; 3,019 HN posts for 96 projects
relevance: Cross-posting a launch to HN roughly doubles short-run star velocity when it lands.

claim: OpenAI announced its GPT-4o 'Spring Update' ahead of time as a livestream for Monday 13 May 2024 at 10am PT, and Sam Altman posted a vague teaser beforehand ('not GPT-5, not a search engine... feels like magic').
testable_trait: Launch post timestamp falls 09:00-11:00 Pacific on a weekday; same account (or CEO account) has a link-free teaser post 1-3 days earlier containing a date/time.
note: Winner-only description; no comparison against un-teased launches.

claim: OpenAI scheduled the GPT-4o event the day before Google I/O 2024, i.e. deliberately counter-programming a rival's news day rather than avoiding it.
testable_trait: untestable (needs an external calendar of competitor events); partially testable as 'launch within 48h of another corpus account's launch'.
note: Contradicts the generic 'avoid big-news days' advice; large labs can counter-programme, small startups probably cannot.

claim: After the GPT-4o stream Sam Altman posted the single word 'her', a one-word cultural-reference post from the CEO account that became the meme of the launch.
testable_trait: CEO/founder account posts a very short (<20 chars) text-only post within 6h of the company launch post; compare its engagement with the main post.

claim: GPT-5's launch livestream (Aug 2025) showed mis-scaled benchmark bar charts (a 69.1% bar drawn the same height as 30.8%; a 47.4% bar taller than 50%); Altman called it a 'mega chart screwup' and staff apologised for 'chart crime' - benchmark charts are the most scrutinised launch asset.
source: Tech.co / PC Gamer / Futurism, 2025, press article
testable_trait: Launch post has an image and text with benchmark terms (SWE-bench, %, SOTA); high reply:like or quote:repost ratio as a proxy for critical pile-on.
note: Shows a failure mode, not a success factor.

claim: xAI launched Grok 3 (Feb 2025) by livestream on X with a 'world's smartest AI' claim; its benchmark chart was publicly disputed by OpenAI employees (omitted o3-mini-high comparison), so competitor-employee quote-posts became part of the launch's distribution.
testable_trait: Launch post text names a competitor model; count of quote-posts from accounts belonging to competitor organisations in the corpus.

claim: DeepSeek released R1 on 20 Jan 2025 with weights under the MIT licence and claims of parity with OpenAI o1 at far lower cost; Marc Andreessen praised it on X as 'a profound gift to the world' and the app reached No.1 on the US App Store by 27 Jan.
source: TechSpot / TechNode / deepseek.com, 2025, press article + company post
testable_trait: Text contains open-weights terms (open source, MIT, Apache, weights) and/or a huggingface.co / github.com link; number of quote-posts by corpus accounts with >500k followers within 7 days.
note: Spread took ~a week and was driven by third parties, not by the lab's own post; causal role of the open licence is inferred.

claim: Mistral released Mistral 7B (Sept 2023) by posting a bare BitTorrent magnet link with no paper, blog or marketing copy; the minimalism itself was covered as a stunt.
source: pnote.eu newsletter / Import AI (Jack Clark), 2023, newsletter
testable_trait: Launch post text length <60 chars and consists mainly of a link/URI, no media.
note: Winner-only; works for a lab with pre-existing researcher reputation.

claim: Black Forest Labs launched FLUX.1 (1 Aug 2024) in three tiers (API-only [pro], open-weight non-commercial [dev], Apache-2.0 [schnell]) with day-one availability on Hugging Face, Replicate, fal.ai and ComfyUI, so partners had their own reason to post on launch day.
testable_trait: Launch post @mentions >=2 partner/hosting accounts; those accounts quote or repost within 24h.
note: No engagement numbers found for the X post.

claim: Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B (released Fri 14 Aug 2026, Apache 2.0) became the No.1 trending model on Hugging Face and passed 3 million downloads in three days.
source: Cybernews / Alibaba Cloud blog, 2026, press article
testable_trait: Text contains licence name + huggingface.co link; posted Friday (tests whether weekday rule matters for open-weights drops).
note: Friday release contradicts the Tuesday-morning rule.

claim: Meta released Llama 3.1 405B (July 2024) together with a Mark Zuckerberg open letter arguing for open-source AI, and cited 300M+ cumulative Llama downloads as the proof number.
testable_trait: CEO account posts a long-form post/Article within 1h of the company launch post; launch text contains a cumulative-usage number.
note: Download figure is self-reported.

claim: Google's 'nano-banana' image model first appeared anonymously on LMArena (Aug 2025), went viral among users, was teased by Demis Hassabis and other leaders with banana emoji on X, then launched as Gemini 2.5 Flash Image; Google later said 10M+ users were new to Gemini and 200M+ images were edited.
source: Google blog / Axios, 2025, company blog + press
testable_trait: Executive accounts post emoji-only or <30-char text-only teasers 1-7 days before the company's launch post; launch post follows with media.
note: User numbers are Google's own.

claim: OpenAI launched the Sora app (30 Sept 2025) invite-only in the US and Canada; it hit No.1 on the US App Store on 3 Oct, reached 1M downloads in under five days (627k iOS installs in week one vs 606k for ChatGPT's first week), codes resold for ~$45 on eBay, and the Sora lead used the milestone post to promise 'more invite codes soon'.
testable_trait: Text contains 'invite' / 'invite code' / 'waitlist'; follow-up milestone post within 7 days from an employee account that quotes the launch post.
note: Incumbent with 100M+ existing users; not transferable evidence for a startup.

claim: When GPT-4o image generation launched (25 Mar 2025) Sam Altman switched his profile picture to a Ghibli-style portrait and two days later posted 'our GPUs are melting' while announcing rate limits - a capacity-scarcity follow-up that itself became news.
testable_trait: Same or CEO account posts a follow-up within 72h mentioning demand/capacity/rate limits/GPUs; engagement of follow-up relative to launch post.

claim: Anthropic introduced Claude Code on 24 Feb 2025 as a 'limited research preview' bundled into the Claude 3.7 Sonnet model announcement rather than as a separate launch.
testable_trait: Launch text contains 'research preview' / 'preview' / 'beta'; single post announces >1 product.
note: No X engagement data located.

claim: For Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024) an Anthropic developer-relations lead posted his own thread on X showing coding ability, which press quoted alongside power users' reactions - employee demo threads are a routine second wave of a lab launch.
testable_trait: Number of employee-account posts that quote the company launch post within 1h/24h; whether those are threads (self-reply chains) with video/image.
note: VentureBeat itself notes the employee is 'obviously biased'.

claim: At Sora's first reveal (Feb 2024) Sam Altman invited prompts in replies on X and posted generated videos back, turning the reply section into a live demo.
testable_trait: CEO post asks for prompts ('reply with'); followed by >=3 media posts from the same account within 6h (reply bodies not in corpus, so only partially testable).
note: from memory - not confirmed by search in this session.

claim: StackBlitz launched Bolt.new on 3 Oct 2024 'with a single tweet' from CEO Eric Simons after stalling at $0.7M ARR; it reported $4M ARR about four weeks later, $20M at ~2-3 months and $40M at five months.
source: Growth Unhinged (Kyle Poyar) interview / Anthropic customer story, 2025, newsletter
testable_trait: Launch originates from founder personal account, not company account; single post rather than thread; contains demo video.
note: Classic survivorship case: revenue is self-reported and the same team had years of unsuccessful launches before it.

claim: Bolt's CEO posted a '$0 to $4M ARR in 4 weeks' case-study tweet on 12 Nov 2024, roughly 40 days after launch - a metrics follow-up reused as a second launch moment.
source: Eric Simons tweet as surfaced in search / Anthropic case study, 2024, founder post
testable_trait: Same account posts a follow-up within 60 days containing a currency/ARR/user number and quoting or linking the original launch post.

claim: Supabase's Launch Week ships one major feature or announcement per day for a week on a fixed ~3-month cadence; features are often shipped earlier and only marketed during the week.
testable_trait: Company account has >=4 distinct launch posts on consecutive weekdays, each with its own media; text contains 'Launch Week' / 'Day N'.
note: Described by the winner; Supabase reports an 'immediate uptick' but no X metrics.

claim: Supabase's published launch-day run-of-show: reminder tweet 7:30, Product Hunt live 7:55, blog 8:00, launch tweet 8:05, tweet shared with technical angel investors 8:10, Twitter Space 8:15 - i.e. investor amplification is scheduled five minutes after the post.
testable_trait: Count of quote-posts/reposts by other corpus accounts within 10/30/60 minutes of the launch post.
note: Supabase says angel boosts 'increased acquisition' without numbers.

claim: Supabase advises repeating launches because 'we often overestimate the reach of our online marketing efforts' - many people miss the first announcement.
testable_trait: Account re-posts or quote-posts its own launch post 1-14 days later; engagement of the re-post vs original.

claim: Supabase issues shareable Launch Week tickets (auto-generated images with the user's GitHub avatar) and for Launch Week 7 offered better odds in a keyboard prize draw for sharing the ticket on Twitter and LinkedIn.
testable_trait: Text contains giveaway/prize terms ('win', 'giveaway', 'ticket'); volume of third-party posts linking the same domain in the pre-launch week.
note: Share-for-prize mechanics now sit close to X's engagement-solicitation rules (see PB records on engagement bait).

claim: launchweek.dev counted 126 launch weeks run by 94 companies in 2024; only 7 companies (7.4%) ran three or more; one participant (Bucket) reported 15x reach after announcing its week two weeks ahead.
source: fmerian on DEV.to citing launchweek.dev, 2025, practitioner blog
testable_trait: Company account posts a launch-week announcement 7-14 days before a burst of >=4 launch posts.
note: Prevalence count, not an effectiveness study.

claim: Lovable describes two earlier launches under the name 'GPT Engineer' as failures; the third (Nov 2024) combined a rename, a Supabase integration and co-marketing, a Product Hunt launch with promo video, and direct outreach to X influencers and communities.
testable_trait: Same account has >=2 launch posts for the same product months apart; later one @mentions an integration partner account.
note: Rare within-company before/after, but product, name and market timing all changed together.

claim: Lovable's open-source predecessor repo gpt-engineer reached tens of thousands of GitHub stars (20k 'almost overnight'; 40-50k later by other sources) and built a ~27k waitlist before the commercial launch.
source: Postbeam GTM breakdown / Sacra, 2025, secondary analysis
testable_trait: Launch post links github.com; text contains 'open source'; star-count number in text.
note: Star counts differ between sources.

claim: Cursor's CEO says the team 'lived like monks' in 2023 and that the product 'spread from word of mouth' after an initial social push to build a waitlist; developers posting their own screenshots and clips were the distribution.
source: Michael Truell interview as reported (AOL/Business Insider syndication), 2025, press article
testable_trait: Ratio of third-party posts @mentioning the product account to the company's own posts in the 30 days after launch.
note: 'No marketing' is the company's own framing; unquantified.

claim: Cognition's Devin launch video (12 Mar 2024) opens with the disruption hook 'the first AI software engineer', shows highlights rather than a tutorial, puts a founder on camera, and uses SWE-bench (13.86%) and founder credentials (IOI golds) for trust; valuation went from $350M to $2B within a month.
source: Sally Liu, 'Anatomy of a Viral Product Video', 2025, Substack analysis
testable_trait: Launch post has native video; text begins 'Introducing' / 'Meet'; text contains 'first' or a benchmark name/percentage.
note: View counts conflict (1.1M for one cut vs ~31M claimed for the tweet). Answer.ai later found Devin completed 3 of 20 tasks.

claim: On Devin's demo day Cognition reposted 15 endorsing tweets from accounts with ~3M combined followers, and only 5 of the 15 showed signs of having used the product.
testable_trait: Number of third-party posts reposted by the launching account within 24h; summed follower count of quote-posting corpus accounts.
note: Strongest documented example of coordinated/curated same-day endorsement.

claim: Devin was announced with request-access only and did not reach general availability until Dec 2024 (about nine months later, at $500/month).
source: Sally Liu / The Register, 2025, analysis + press
testable_trait: Launch text contains 'request access' / 'waitlist' / 'early access' and no pricing line.
note: Demo-first, access-later worked for fundraising, later drew 'staged demo' criticism.

claim: Leading with 'open-source alternative to X' is a standard dev-tool positioning line; Supabase's 'open source Firebase alternative' is the usual example and is how developers find it by search.
source: Pristren blog / DEV.to and HackerNoon founder posts, 2024-2026, practitioner blogs
testable_trait: Text matches 'alternative to <Name>' or '<Name> killer' or @mentions a larger competitor account.
note: Only winners are cited.

claim: A dev-tool growth roundup claims Linear's founders built a ~10K waitlist from their Twitter followings and Resend's founder a 20K+ waitlist from open-source work and Twitter before launch.
source: kendo-hq 'dev tool growth playbooks', undated, marketing blog
testable_trait: Founder account follower count at launch; presence of a waitlist-link post >=30 days before the launch post.
note: Single low-authority source; no primary confirmation found.

claim: Cluely's launch video was posted from founder Roy Lee's own X account on 20 Apr 2025 with the caption 'Cluely is out. cheat on everything.' and showed 13.2M views as of Oct 2026; a $5.3M seed was announced the next day.
source: viral.app sourced breakdown / TechCrunch, 2025-2026, vendor analysis + press
testable_trait: Founder account; text <60 chars, lowercase, no link; native video with a human on camera (media type video); funding post within 48h.
note: No source says whether the X post was boosted; view count is the public counter.

claim: Roy Lee states the strategy as provocation: 'algorithms promote the most controversial things' and 'if half the audience doesn't hate it, it's not viral enough'; Cluely later repositioned from 'cheat on everything' to an AI meeting note-taker (Nov 2025) and in Mar 2026 retracted a $7M ARR claim (June 2025 ARR was $5.2M).
source: a16z podcast via TechCrunch; viral.app timeline, 2025-2026, press + vendor analysis
testable_trait: High reply:like ratio and quote:repost ratio (controversy proxy); negative-sentiment words in text.
note: Views did not translate into the claimed revenue; winner-told and partly retracted.

claim: Cluely said in July 2025 that it had 700+ clippers paid '$0 per video' plus a bonus per 1,000 views, producing 100M views 'in a matter of weeks', alongside 60+ in-house creators and 50 interns at $50/hour - i.e. most of its view volume was bought per view, mainly on TikTok and Instagram.
source: Roy Lee thread / SF Standard via viral.app, 2025, founder post + press
testable_trait: untestable on X corpus directly (clips are posted by unaffiliated accounts); proxy: many low-follower accounts posting the same video/URL within days.
note: Reported view totals are explicitly paid-for views.

claim: Clippers are typically paid $0.50-$2 per thousand views; Cluely, Lovable, 1X and Nothing are named as having hired them, and a marketplace (Clip) reports $4M+ paid across 900+ campaigns.
source: TBPN Digest commentary, Aug 2025; Digiday 'WTF is clipping', 2025, press/commentary
testable_trait: untestable (payment not observable); proxy: duplicate media hashes across unrelated accounts.
note: Treat any 'tens of millions of views' claim from these companies as including purchased views.

claim: Manus's launch demo video (Mar 2025) drew 1M+ views in under 20 hours; access was by invite code, codes were listed for $1,000+ on resale sites, and waitlist claims ranged from 'hundreds of thousands' to 2M in a week.
testable_trait: Text contains 'invite code'; launch video; number of third-party posts containing 'invite code' + product name in following 7 days.
note: Waitlist size and resale prices are disputed; the company denied selling codes.

claim: Press framed Manus against a named rival and price ('challenges OpenAI's $200 agent'), and DeepSeek against o1 - comparison to a named incumbent is the default headline for AI launches.
testable_trait: Launch text names a competitor product or @mentions a competitor account; contains a price comparison.

claim: Rabbit sold out its first 10,000 R1 units in one day after its CES 2024 keynote video (internal goal was 500) and reportedly three batches of 10,000 within four days.
testable_trait: Follow-up post within 48h containing 'sold out' / batch number; launch post with long-form keynote video.

claim: The Rabbit R1 and Humane AI Pin both shipped to harsh reviews in April 2024 (MKBHD: Humane 'the worst product I've ever reviewed', R1 'barely reviewable') - launch-video hype without a working product reversed within months.
testable_trait: untestable in launch-post corpus (needs later product outcomes).
note: Counter-example to survivorship: high launch engagement, failed product.

claim: Friend's founder announced a ~$1M NYC subway ad campaign (11,000+ car cards) in an X post on 25 Sept 2025 that passed 25M views with ~1,000 mostly critical comments; reported unit sales were only ~3,000-5,000.
testable_trait: Reply:like ratio; views-per-follower outlier; image of offline ad in media.
note: Rage-bait reach did not convert to sales at comparable scale.

claim: Pika launched Pika 1.0 on 28 Nov 2023 with a demo reel video, a waitlist link and a same-day $55M funding announcement, bundling product, access and financing news into one moment.
testable_trait: Launch text contains both a funding amount and a waitlist/sign-up link; native video.
note: No reliable view count for the X post found.

claim: The Browser Company teased Dia (Dec 2024) with a video that doubled as a recruiting pitch and included early prototype demos, months before the product was available.
testable_trait: Teaser video post >30 days before launch post from the same account; text contains hiring terms.

claim: Granola grew ~10% week over week after its May 2024 launch 'mostly thanks to word of mouth among VCs and founders', having seeded a closed beta with VCs and tech executives first.
testable_trait: Share of launch-week quote-posts that come from investor accounts in the corpus.

claim: Perplexity's head of growth says roughly 80% of acquisition is organic word of mouth and that paid channels mostly pull forward users who would have arrived anyway.
source: Raman Malik (20VC interview summary), 2025, podcast summary
testable_trait: untestable (needs acquisition attribution data).
note: Self-reported.

claim: Generative-media products spread when the output is a shareable visual 'wow' (image/video); audio products such as Suno or Udio are argued to get less organic attention because the output cannot be seen in a feed.
source: Charlie Graham, 'Going viral with product-led visual wow moments', Substack essay
testable_trait: Media type of launch post (video/image vs none); number of third-party posts with media that @mention the product in week one.
note: Opinion essay.

claim: Robinhood's pre-launch referral waitlist (move up the queue by sharing your link) grew to roughly one million sign-ups before launch.
source: The Growth Playbook Substack and other case studies, secondary analysis
testable_trait: Text contains a referral-style CTA ('share to move up', 'skip the line'); link to waitlist domain.
note: Pre-2022 precedent; winner-only.

claim: Superhuman kept a six-figure waitlist (180k-275k depending on source) behind a mandatory onboarding call; Clubhouse's invite-only hype is the cautionary case - once anyone could join 'there was nothing left to want'.
source: eChai / Sherwood / Femstreet 'velvet rope' essays, secondary analysis
testable_trait: untestable (needs retention after waitlist opens).
note: Waitlist numbers conflict across sources.

claim: YC's Kat Manalac teaches launching as a repeated tactic, not a one-off: most first launches are ignored, so launch to friends/family, then each community you belong to, then again for each feature or milestone; write like you talk and keep copy very tight.
source: Kat Manalac, 'How to Launch (Again and Again)', YC Startup School 2019, YC library talk (read via third-party transcript summaries)
testable_trait: Number of distinct launch-type posts per account per quarter; launch post word count; absence of marketing adjectives.
note: Original ycombinator.com page not opened; content confirmed via transcript summaries.

claim: YC opened 'Launch YC' publicly in June 2022: a leaderboard where YC companies can launch on any day at any time; YC says it encourages founders to launch on many platforms (YC Directory, Product Hunt, Hacker News, Launch YC).
source: TechCrunch quoting YC's Lindsay Amos, 2022, press article
testable_trait: Launch text contains 'YC' batch tag (e.g. 'YC W25') or links ycombinator.com/launches; @ycombinator mention.

claim: The 'YC launch video' format circulated in 2025-2026 is about three minutes or less (shorter cuts for social), structured 'hook first, product second, ask last', often phone-shot or screen-recorded and posted by the founder on X; one vendor library lists 160+ such videos.
sample_size: 160+ videos catalogued, no per-video stats published
testable_trait: Native video present; text includes YC batch tag; founder account vs company account.
note: Vendor selling launch videos; the gallery contains only videos chosen for it (survivorship).

claim: Launch-video agencies self-report averages of '100k+' and '400K+ organic' views per video and one '1M+ views in two days' case; no independent count of YC launch-video views was found.
source: Vendor sites (Flowjam and competitors) as returned by search, 2025-2026, vendor marketing
testable_trait: View count on video launch posts normalised by follower count.
note: Self-reported portfolio averages; selection and possible paid amplification not disclosed.

claim: Reported launch-video costs run from ~$1K-3K (Loom-style) through $5K-15K (standard 60-90s agency cut) to $30K-50K+ (premium).
source: Flowjam, 'Product Launch Videos: The 2026 Founder's Playbook', vendor guide
testable_trait: untestable (cost not observable).
note: Vendor price list.

claim: Brex's startup newsletter called it a 'launch video arms race' (Aug 2025): novelty 'erodes fast' amid glossy AI clips, visibility comes from 'scarcity, stakes and status', and the real metric is qualified conversations per dollar, not views.
source: Brex Startup Community newsletter, Aug 2025, vendor newsletter
testable_trait: Trend test: median views-per-follower of video launch posts by quarter 2024-2026.
note: Opinion; testable as a decay hypothesis.

claim: YC deleted its own X/LinkedIn posts of batch company Optifye's demo video (Feb 2025) after it went viral for the wrong reasons ('sweatshops-as-a-service').
testable_trait: Quote:repost ratio >1 on a launch video post (ratio'd).
note: Accelerator-account amplification multiplies backlash as well as reach.

claim: Garry Tan and the YC account do repost/quote founders' launch posts, but no measurement of the lift was found; one documented example totalled only ~2.4K combined views.
source: Digg aggregator item; Forbes Australia profile, 2025-2026, press/aggregator
testable_trait: Launch post quoted/reposted by YC-affiliated corpus accounts; compare views with matched posts from same author not quoted.
note: Commonly assumed benefit with no published evidence - a good candidate for a within-account test.

claim: Product Hunt's official guide: every launch goes live at 12:01am Pacific and runs to midnight; 'there's no magic weekday that guarantees a top spot'; weekdays have more traffic and competition, weekends are quieter on both.
source: Product Hunt Help Center launch guide, current 2026, vendor guide
testable_trait: X post linking producthunt.com timestamped 00:00-02:00 Pacific; day of week.

claim: Product Hunt's official rules: 'Never ask for upvotes' (ask for feedback/comments instead); share the link 'everywhere your audience already is' including X; 'personality travels further than a generic we're-live post'; a famous hunter is not needed; giveaways tied to upvotes and paid votes are banned.
source: Product Hunt Help Center launch guide, current 2026, vendor guide
testable_trait: Posts linking producthunt.com: text contains 'upvote' (rule-breaking) vs 'feedback'/'support'; engagement difference.

claim: An analysis of 4,962 Product Hunt launches (1 Jan-1 Sep 2026) found Tuesday averages 30.4 launches/day vs 10.7 on Saturday, and the median points needed for top-5 were 165 on Saturday, 205 Friday, 210 Tuesday, 220 Monday, 235 Thursday; the author states this is a historical bar, not a causal day effect.
source: Databox maker post on Product Hunt forums, 2026, vendor analysis
testable_trait: Day-of-week of posts linking producthunt.com; competition proxy = number of corpus launch posts same day.
note: Covers top-ranked launches only; cannot separate maker type from weekday.

claim: Marc Lou launched ShipFast on Product Hunt first (about $1,000 in sales in the first seven hours), repeated the launch on Hacker News, and treats every product launch as a public marketing event from his personal X account.
source: Secondary write-ups of Marc Lou; Bootstrapped Founder podcast ep. 300, practitioner/podcast
testable_trait: Founder account posts linking producthunt.com on launch day plus >=2 follow-up posts with sales numbers same day.
note: Figure comes from search summary of secondary sources; exact page not opened.

claim: A study of 1,209 posts from 15 build-in-public creators (2024-Sep 2026) found only 3.6% (43) reached 10x the creator's own median; median engagement rate was 1.60% for text-only, 1.39% image, 1.28% video, 1.01% quote posts, with video earning the most bookmarks.
testable_trait: Outlier = post engagement >=10x author's median; media type; quote vs original.
note: Page returned 403 on fetch; numbers confirmed from search result text only. Authors flag medium confidence.

claim: Across 4,965 startups with verified revenue, those listing an X account with under 100 followers reached $1k/month less often (12.1%, n=1,343) than those listing no X account at all (17.9%, n=1,163).
source: Indie Hackers post (author's own database), 2026, founder analysis
testable_trait: Follower count bucket of launching account vs launch-post engagement.
note: Outcome is revenue, not post reach; confounded by founder type.

claim: Tony Dinh announced TypingMind primarily through his own X account built by 'building interesting stuff and sharing it in public'; reported revenue was ~$22K in the first week.
source: Starter Story / Indie Hackers founder post, 2023-2024, founder interview
testable_trait: Founder account with prior high posting cadence; launch post contains price; follow-up revenue post within 7 days.
note: Self-reported revenue; figures differ slightly across sources.

claim: Danny Postma's earlier product Headlime grew from $1K to $20K MRR between Dec and Feb 2021 after his tweets about learnings, numbers and progress went viral and attracted larger accounts.
testable_trait: Text contains MRR/revenue figure with currency symbol; image attachment (screenshot); quoted by larger accounts.
note: Pre-2022; self-reported.

claim: Marc Lou publishes monthly revenue by product on X (e.g. $66,040 in Oct 2025), and after a Pieter Levels tweet about fake revenue screenshots he built a verified-revenue tool in a day that reportedly made $20,378 the next day - revenue screenshots are common enough, and faked often enough, to support a verification product.
testable_trait: Text contains '$' + number + 'MRR'/'revenue'/'/mo'; image attached; posted in first 5 days of month.
note: Revenue numbers in posts cannot be verified from the corpus.

claim: Arvid Kahl argued in April 2026 that the copycat risk of building in public, which he used to consider manageable below ~$20-30K MRR, has 'collapsed to zero' with AI cloning, turning it into careful risk management rather than a default.
source: Arvid Kahl, The Bootstrapped Founder ep. 439, 2026, podcast/essay
testable_trait: untestable (needs clone/competitor data).
note: A practitioner who benefited from the tactic now advising caution.

claim: Pieter Levels posts live revenue/MRR figures and Stripe screenshots for products such as Photo AI from his personal account, with copycats appearing but speed and audience keeping him ahead.
source: From memory; one unverified secondary summary seen in search
testable_trait: Text contains '$' + 'MRR'; image attached; founder account.
note: from memory - no primary source opened this session.

claim: Buffer's analysis of 18.8M X posts from 71,000 accounts found link posts are the worst-performing format: median engagement rate ~0% for non-Premium accounts since March 2025, and ~0.28% for Premium accounts vs ~0.90% text, ~0.85% video, ~0.42% image (Aug 2025).
source: Buffer (Julian Winternheimer), Oct 2025, vendor data study
testable_trait: has_link (external URL in post body) vs none; stratify by verified/Premium status and media type.
note: Correlational; Buffer did NOT test link-in-reply, it only suggests it. Not launch-specific.

claim: X's head of product Nikita Bier said in Oct 2025 'links are not deboosted' and in Apr 2026 recommended putting links in the post body with context; Elon Musk said in July 2026 that X has not penalised links 'for over a year'.
source: PPC Land / Free Press Journal reporting on X posts, 2025-2026, press article
testable_trait: has_link in body vs link absent with a self-reply shortly after (reply bodies not in corpus: only self-reply existence is testable); compare by half-year 2024-2026.
note: Platform statements conflict with Buffer's observational data; 'link in reply' is probably a stale tactic but the data are not conclusive.

claim: Buffer's timing analysis (8.7M tweets per the article body; headline says 1M) puts the best slots at Tuesday 9am and Wednesday 9-10am local time, Tue-Thu as best days, Saturday worst and evenings 6-11pm worst.
source: Buffer (Kirsti Lang), Mar 2026, vendor data study
testable_trait: Local/Pacific hour and weekday of post vs engagement rate, controlling for author.
note: Engagement rate, not reach; time-zone normalisation unexplained; Buffer sells scheduling. General posts, not launches.

claim: A launch-video vendor reports that Tuesday/Wednesday 8am ET launch tweets got 3-5x the median impressions of other slots across 79 founder tweets, and that Saturday afternoon got ~10-15x less.
testable_trait: Weekday x hour bucket of launch posts vs views per follower.
note: Unpublished data from a vendor; founders who pick Tuesday morning may differ systematically.

claim: Buffer's 2025 timing study (1M+ posts) also reported text posts getting ~30% more engagement than video posts and ~37% more than image posts on X.
testable_trait: Media type (none/image/video) vs engagement rate, within author.
note: Runs against 'a launch needs a video'; engagement rate is not views, and launches are a special case.

claim: Vendor guidance on launch videos: 45-90 seconds (top-reach 2026 cuts 60-75s), open on the pain point not the logo (logo-first opens lose 40-60% of viewers before the product appears), upload natively (external video links cost 60-80% of reach), and video launch tweets do ~4:1 vs no video.
testable_trait: Native video vs external video link vs no video; (video duration only if present in media metadata).
note: No sample sizes; vendor with a commercial interest.

claim: One startup (Origami) paid $3,000 for a block of 20 creators to amplify in the first hour and got 250,000 views in that hour; the vendor says the video alone did not do this, and recommends 15-30 creators in the first hour.
testable_trait: Number of quote-posts/reposts from accounts >10k followers within first 60 minutes; whether those accounts have no prior interaction with the author (paid-seeding proxy).
note: Explicitly paid amplification: the reported view count is not organic.

claim: A launch-video teardown advises cutting a separate <=15-second version if the post will be promoted with X ads, indicating that paid boosting of launch posts is normal practice.
testable_trait: untestable (promotion not visible in public data); proxy: views very high relative to likes+reposts+replies.

claim: X counts a video view at 2 seconds with 50% of the player in view, and Media Studio reports organic and promoted views separately to the owner while the public counter shows one number - so public view counts cannot distinguish paid from organic.
source: X Help Center, Media Studio analytics, platform documentation
testable_trait: views / (likes+reposts+replies) ratio as anomaly flag for boosted posts.
note: Whether promoted impressions are included in the public count was not confirmed by a source; treat large view counts as suspect either way.

claim: X said in March 2026 it was close to having Grok detect posts that 'directly solicit engagement' and push them down in ranking; by mid-2026 accounts that repeatedly solicit engagement could be removed from creator revenue share.
source: PiunikaWeb / Kompozy reporting Nikita Bier's posts, 2026, press article
testable_trait: Text regex for solicitation CTAs: 'comment X and I'll DM', 'reply for access', 'RT for invite', 'like + repost'; compare engagement before vs after Mar 2026.
note: No published penalty size. 'Comment for access' is common in AI demo posts but no effectiveness data was found.

claim: X purged 1.7M reply-spam bots in Oct 2025 and in Jan 2026 revoked API access for 'InfoFi' apps that pay users to post, citing AI slop and reply spam - paid-to-post and pod-style schemes are an enforcement target.
testable_trait: Burst of near-identical quote-posts from low-follower accounts in first hour (pod proxy).

claim: Founder-led posting is the standard advice (post the launch from the founder's personal account; company account reposts), and the biggest startup cases here (Bolt, Cluely) did launch from founder accounts, but no controlled comparison on X was found - the only quantified reach gap (5.61% vs 0.8%) is a Socialinsider LinkedIn figure.
source: Stackmatix founder-led X playbook and similar guides, 2025-2026, vendor guides
testable_trait: Is launch post authored by a person account or the organisation account; does the other one quote/repost within 1h; engagement per follower for each.
note: Labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) launch from the company account with executives quote-posting, the reverse pattern.

claim: a16z set up a 'New Media' team (announced Nov 2025) offering portfolio companies 'Launch as a Service' - social copy, rollout timing, launch videos and amplification through a16z-owned channels, prioritising X.
source: a16z New Media pages and commentary, 2025-2026, investor marketing
testable_trait: Launch post quoted/reposted by investor-firm accounts and partners within 1h.
note: Evidence of effect is a16z's own testimonials.

claim: Supabase's own data point for investor amplification: technical angel investors boosted the Auth announcement on social media, which the company says increased acquisition and activation.
testable_trait: Count of quote-posts from investor accounts in corpus in first hour.
note: No numbers given.

claim: Pre-announcement is used at every scale: OpenAI's dated livestream notice, Google executives' emoji teasers, Bucket's two-weeks-ahead launch-week notice, Dia's months-ahead teaser video.
source: Synthesis of cases above (VentureBeat, Google blog, DEV.to, TechCrunch)
testable_trait: Existence of a teaser post (no link, future date/time or 'tomorrow'/'soon') from the same account 1-14 days before the launch post; compare launch engagement with vs without, within account.
note: All four are successes; nobody writes up teased launches that flopped.

claim: Follow-up posts are part of the working pattern: Sora's '#1 on the App Store, more invite codes soon', Rabbit's 'sold out in 24 hours, 20x our goal', Bolt's '$4M ARR in 4 weeks', Altman's 'GPUs are melting'.
source: Synthesis of cases above (TechCrunch, TechSpot, Growth Unhinged, Fortune)
testable_trait: Same author posts within 1-30 days a post containing a number + milestone word (sold out, #1, ARR, users, downloads) that quotes or follows the launch post.
note: Only launches that had a milestone can post one - pure survivorship.
